title: Continuity of enlarged etale base change
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let X,Y be algebraic spaces over S [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let f:X → Y. On the enlarged etale sites of chartwise etale algebraic spaces, with jointly surjective chartwise etale coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], the actual sheaf-fibre-product functor V ↦ X ×_Y V is continuous: precomposing any sheaf on the enlarged site of X yields a sheaf on the enlarged site of Y.

proof.text: Prove chartwise cancellation directly from [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] and [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection]. The actual sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] then provide enlarged pullbacks. The identity object is terminal; the inclusion into the slice of ambient sheaves preserves these limits and is fully faithful. Base change agrees with ambient slice pullback up to pullback symmetry, so it preserves finite limits. These arguments are local proved subarguments and avoid importing the downstream scheme-density module.

source.place: Tag 03G2, proof of part (1): base change on spaces-etale sites.

proof.text: Covering pullbacks and composition are verified by lifting field-valued sections. Use the isomorphism and composition clauses of [lem-trf-presheaf-field-lift-family-calculus] for the site axioms. For the image of a cover under base change, lift its original component after a field extension, restrict the other component to that field, and combine them by the sheaf pullback universal property. Naturality gives compatibility. Chartwise cancellation gives etaleness of all enlarged arrows. The same argument proves stability under every choice of enlarged covering pullbacks, including empty families.

source.place: Tag 03G2, proof of part (1): base change on spaces-etale sites.

proof.text: Express an arbitrary covering presieve by its arrows and pull it back along an arbitrary arrow using the explicit enlarged pullbacks. The preceding field-lifting calculation gives a covering family. The fibre-product functor preserves its pairwise pullbacks by finite-limit preservation. Apply Presieve.IsSheafFor.comp_iff_of_preservesPairwisePullbacks and the precoverage generated-topology sheaf criterion to each sheaf. This proves continuity of the exact published base-change functor.
